corrections.description: Phrases containing the names of private individuals appeared in the synchronized-phrase table, in per-phrase adoption-curve pages, in the receipts of one talking point, and in the Democratic composite for this day (and in table rows on 2026-07-09). OnScript measures elected officials' public statements and does not rank, page, quote or narrate private citizens. Every citation involved was valid and every number was correct — the citation verifier has no opinion about privacy, by construction, so no receipts audit could have caught this.
corrections.resolution: Those phrase families are withheld from every published surface and their pages have been removed. The affected composite was re-composed from the same day's measured statistics by the deterministic composer, with every other number unchanged, and is now labelled 'deterministic template (not a language model)' on the page. The underlying record of what members said is retained unaltered (Art. VI); only this instrument's ranking of it is withheld. Suppression is content-neutral protection applied identically to both parties — it is not a finding, and no threshold was changed.

corrections.description: Some daily talking points were bound by a connective or attribution phrase rather than a message — e.g. “into the trump administration’s” or “democratic colleagues in demanding the”. Each such key is string-valid (every cited statement contains it verbatim, which is why they clustered) and cleared the >=3 quorum, but the shared span is grammar, not a shared message, so the receipts pointed at unrelated topics. The citation verifier checks verbatim-ness, quorum and attribution — not whether the shared span is a message — so no receipts audit could have caught it. Flagged talking points: 19 across 7 day(s), categorized by reason (18 incomplete syntactic span, 1 attribution frame), both parties (15 D / 4 R — the gate is party-blind; the skew tracks the caucus).
corrections.resolution: A deterministic, party-blind key-admission gate now rejects connective/attribution scaffold keys at generation (run_assemble), and the quorum now counts only distinct document families whose source actually carries the key, so transitively-chained interlopers no longer count toward it. Already-published days are corrected at render time (the same display-time refresh the privacy guard uses): the affected talking points are dropped from every page, and where a day's composite had narrated one, the composite is re-derived from that day's surviving measured statistics by the deterministic composer and labelled 'deterministic template (not a language model)' — the same trusted degradation path used for privacy corrections. No number was changed and no record altered; the underlying statements are retained unaltered (Art. VI). The gate is applied identically to both parties (Art. IV).

corrections.description: The composite Daily Lines and talking points for two already-published days went MISSING from this site. The daily collection run rewrites the day record it is working on, and when it landed on a day that had already been published it overwrote that day's composite half with nothing — deleting the two party composites, their talking points, and the day's cross-party phrase pairings. Nothing published was WRONG: no number changed, no citation broke, and the underlying record of what members actually said was never touched. Content that had been published simply stopped being there, and one day's page went on displaying composites whose backing data had been removed. Because every surviving number stayed correct, no receipts audit or citation check could have surfaced this — it is an absence, and the verifier has no opinion about absence. It was found by the pre-launch health review, before this site had an audience.
corrections.resolution: Both days were restored from the exact content originally published, read back out of this project's version history — not regenerated. That distinction is the point: re-running the composer today would have written new prose, under a newer model and a newer prompt, and presented it as what we said on those dates. The restored text is byte-for-byte what was published, including one day whose composite was always a deterministic template rather than a language model, which is labelled as such. A third day (2026-07-09) was deliberately NOT 'restored': it never carried composites, because the composer never ran for it, and manufacturing one now would invent a record rather than repair it — it remains listed as a phrases-only day. The cause is closed in code: a day that has been published is now immutable to the collection run, which skips it and says so, and the only path that may write to a published day is the explicit repair path. Both parties, one rule, no threshold changed.

corrections.description: A phrase containing the name of a private individual — a person named in members' statements about a fatal law-enforcement incident — appeared in the synchronized-phrase table on that day's page, on the phrases index, and on the home page. OnScript measures elected officials' public statements and does not rank or page private citizens, regardless of how newsworthy the underlying event is. A different name-window form of the same name was already withheld, but the suppression list did not carry every window an n-gram can slide across, so this form was not matched. Every citation involved was valid and every number was correct — the citation verifier has no opinion about privacy, by construction, so no receipts audit could have caught this.
corrections.resolution: The remaining name-window forms are now withheld from every published surface and the affected rows no longer render. The underlying record of what members said is retained unaltered (Art. VI); only this instrument's ranking of it is withheld. Suppression is content-neutral protection applied identically to both parties — it is not a finding, and no threshold was changed.

corrections.description: Some daily composite claims attached the size of a transitively connected topic cluster to a verbatim phrase carried by only part of that cluster, while the three displayed receipts could support a different phrase from the same cluster. The composite quote appeared in all three receipts in 2 of 38 stored blocks and in none of them in 14 of 38. The rendered label was absent from at least one receipt in 28 of 63 blocks. The two complete misses were the Democratic block on 2026-07-15 and the Republican block on 2026-07-22. The same code and the same correction apply to both parties.
corrections.resolution: Each new talking point now has one support phrase. Its count is the number of distinct joint-aware units whose statements contain that phrase; its quote comes from a fragment containing the phrase; and its citations come from the same supporting units, with the phrase visible in every receipt. The verifier binds each composite quote to that talking point instead of accepting a match anywhere in the day's fragment pool. Stored day records, composite prose, and the signed post archive remain unchanged. Affected historical receipt blocks carry a deterministic correction note, and this entry covers the uneditable posted threads.

corrections.description: The published instrument fingerprint misdescribed the live measurement instrument. Its method-version registry attested document-families-v1 and surface-eligibility-v2 while the running modules were at document-families-v2 and surface-eligibility-v3, and its schema-version registry attested corrections schema 2 while the running schema was 3. The registry held hand-copied version strings rather than reading them from the owning modules, so it went stale when later work advanced those modules. The fingerprint also keyed code identity on the repository commit, which data commits move, so one measurement could carry a different identity on its day record than on its post manifest. The 2026-07-25 day record and post manifest are the committed instances. Every number and every citation on those surfaces was correct. The defect was in how the instrument described itself, not in any measurement.
corrections.detection_method: Third external adversarial review, verified against the live pipeline modules and the committed 2026-07-25 records.
corrections.resolution: The fingerprint now reads every method and schema version from its owning module, so its attestation cannot drift from the running instrument, and a provider-discovery test fails when a production method module is not registered. Code identity is now a content hash over the measurement tree, which is the pipeline code, prompts, configuration, taxonomy, and schemas, and excludes data and site output, so a data commit does not change it. The fingerprint is stamped once at assembly and the post manifest and the exports inherit those exact bytes. No measurement changed. This correction renders at the next production cycle.
corrections.root_cause: The instrument fingerprint held hand-copied method and schema version strings instead of reading them from the owning modules, and it keyed code identity on the repository commit, which data commits move.

corrections.description: Three published phrase pages claimed the citation quorum on two source units rather than three. Pages 007eacff261c652d (airport to rehabilitate), 2dc5adb851e6e29d (to deliver for our), and e0b16e162cdabc40 (fought to ensure) each showed grounded_units 3, the exact floor, and two of the three receipts on each page were the same 2026-07-09 Nevada airports announcement, published by the Cortez Masto office and the Rosen office with the name order swapped. Measured similarity between the two texts was 0.647 against a near-duplicate bar of 0.72. Every receipt on those pages is a real, verified, correctly quoted source; the defect is the count, which credited one announcement twice and so let three pages rest on two independent offices. Across the 540 published evidence records, 89 carried an uncollapsed same-day cosigned pair and the other 86 remain above the quorum after the collapse. No composite claim, no posted thread, and no cross-party number is affected.
corrections.detection_method: Fifth external adversarial review (docs/39, finding C1), verified against the committed 2026-08-09 phrase evidence slice and the two cited source releases.
corrections.resolution: The near-joint identity that owns document collapse now recognizes cosigned releases: a pair the near-duplicate retrieval already paired, published the same day by two offices whose headlines each name the other member, is one project unit. The decision is a boolean on reciprocal headline naming, so no threshold moved and the citation quorum stays at three. The method version is bumped at the owning stage and inherited by the evidence slice, which invalidates every cached count measured under the superseded collapse. The three pages fall to two grounded units and lose their evidentiary section at the next production cycle; permanent phrase pages remain, without the quorum claim.
corrections.root_cause: The project unit key collapsed joint releases but not cosigned ones. A cosigned release is one announcement that two offices publish under their own letterheads, each with its own dateline, name order, and member quote, so the two texts diverge below the near-duplicate similarity bar and were counted as two independent units. The standing rule that joint and cosigned releases count once through the unit key was therefore enforced for the joint half only.

corrections.description: One paragraph of the essay The First Thing We Did Was Audit Ourselves said a related measure shows the Democratic phrase tightness concentrating in the 2023 to 2025 House-minority years, and promised a September follow-up on power position. No measure that stays inside one data source shows that concentration. The essay's own finding (S1.9) is unaffected. No daily record is affected.
corrections.detection_method: Pre-publication reads of two later essays, verified against the within-lane revalidation rows for S1.4 in docs/13-SEARCH-LEDGER.md.
corrections.resolution: The paragraph was rewritten to say the power-position question is unanswered, the promise of a follow-up was removed, and a dated correction note was added at the foot of the essay. The S1.4 finding card now carries a superseded block pointing at the governing ledger rows.
corrections.root_cause: The essay cited the S1.4 finding card, written before the 2021-01-03 provenance seam was found. The within-lane revalidation refuted the verbatim measure in both lanes and found the density-controlled measure underpowered in both. The card was never updated, and the essay cited the card instead of the ledger.

corrections.description: The fourteen daily records from 2026-10-28 through 2026-11-10, which include Election Day and the week after it, were not measured as they happened. They were assembled on 2026-11-11 from the same public source record, with the same prompts, thresholds and code the freeze had locked. Four things about them differ from an ordinary day. First, none of the fourteen was posted to Bluesky; they are site-only by ruling. Second, 2026-11-03 was published by an explicit repair run that bypasses the readiness gate: it held 25 statements, at most about 31 percent of its same-weekday baseline, a share the gate would have held back and force-finalized with a flag. Third, the records from 2026-10-28 through 2026-11-09 lack the legacy metrics block the collect stage normally writes; that block is not shown on any page. Fourth, the unpublished silence boards for 2026-10-28 through 2026-11-04 were not built. Thirteen of the assemble manifests record a manual run; the manifest for 2026-11-05 records a scheduled run on 2026-11-11.
corrections.detection_method: Operator status review on 2026-11-10. The dead-man notifications had fired throughout and were not recognized as an outage during the election freeze.
corrections.resolution: All seven workflows are pinned to ubuntu-24.04, and a test fails if any workflow returns to a floating image. The fourteen days were assembled and published on 2026-11-11 and are permanently withheld from posting. Each affected day page links this entry. The missing metrics block and silence boards are not rebuilt. The block is a snapshot written once, on the first pass over a day that is still filling in, and it cannot be reproduced after the fact; a later recomputation would write numbers production never wrote. It is shown on no page. (Amended 2026-11-21: this entry first said a repair was scheduled.)
corrections.root_cause: The workflows ran on the floating ubuntu-latest image. On 2026-10-28 that image moved to Ubuntu 26.04, which did not provide the pinned Python 3.12.10, so every run failed at setup. From 2026-10-28T23:21Z to 2026-11-11T14:51Z, 78 workflow runs failed, 26 were skipped, and none succeeded.

corrections.description: Since the ledger's first build, any phrase used in 2 of those 31 or 36 statements was removed from the whole ledger, whatever its share among the roughly 75,000 statements of the 119th Congress. Rebuilt from the raw mirror through 2026-07-09, 89 phrases were removed this way (27 by the Democratic stratum, 63 by the Republican, one by both); each reached the three-office floor on at least one day, 82 of them for Democrats and 81 for Republicans. They are generic phrases such as "look forward to working with" and "house of representatives". None has a phrase page or a phrase-evidence entry. None would have entered the repeated-phrase table of 2026-06-30, the only published day in the rebuilt window on which any of them reached the floor (that table's smallest row held 9 offices; the largest restored phrase held 5). Two of them ("the house of representatives", "look forward to working") appear as Daily Line talking-point labels on four published days (2026-07-20, 07-21, 11-04, 11-10); those come from the claim-clustering path, which never read this cap, and do not change. The instrument fingerprint attested a setting the instrument did not apply.
corrections.detection_method: Read-only audit of the 120th Congress turnover (AUDIT-120th, finding F3), verified by rebuilding the phrase ledger from the raw mirror with and without the minimum.
corrections.resolution: The ledger now skips any stratum below 40 documents when it applies the share test. The 40 and the 5 percent are unchanged. The ledger's method version (phrase-ledger-v2) is registered in the instrument fingerprint at its owning stage, and a test now fails if any fingerprinted setting is read by no pipeline module. The 89 phrases return to the ledger at the next production cycle and are measured like any other; published day records are not rewritten.
corrections.root_cause: The phrase ledger drops a phrase as boilerplate when its document-frequency share exceeds 5 percent in any (congress, party) stratum. The setting that keeps a stratum out of that test until it holds 40 documents, BOILERPLATE_DF_MIN_DOCS, was in the configuration and in the published instrument fingerprint, but no code read it. The corpus has held two such strata since it began: 31 Democratic and 36 Republican statements dated 2025-01-01 and 2025-01-02, which belong to the 118th Congress.

corrections.description: Wherever a page printed a count of offices over a party's eligible offices (for example "40 of 257"), the count could include up to three nonvoting offices that the total left out: three Democratic and three Republican delegates are seated. A share could be overstated by at most three offices, a little over one percentage point. Measured from 2025-01-03 to 2026-07-09, a delegate was in the count on 328 of 550 Democratic party-days and 276 of 545 Republican party-days, an average of 0.89 Democratic and 0.66 Republican offices a day. No ranking, threshold or selection used the share, so no phrase, Daily Line or award changes.
corrections.detection_method: Read-only audit of the 120th Congress turnover (AUDIT-120th, finding F5), then measured over the raw mirror from 2025-01-03 to 2026-07-09.
corrections.resolution: The eligible total now includes the seated nonvoting offices, so both sides count one population: 260 Democratic and 272 Republican offices on 2026-11-21, where the pages showed 257 and 269. The voting count is published beside it in the nightly audit. The office count is restricted to offices the roster seats that day, and any other author is counted in a separate field. The method version is date-effective-denominators-v2. Day records already published are not rewritten; the new total applies from the first day assembled after this entry.
corrections.root_cause: The count of a party's offices using a phrase included that party's delegates and resident commissioner when they published. The eligible total it was printed against counted voting members only. The two sides of the fraction used different populations.

corrections.description: On 55 published day pages from 2026-09-01 to 2026-11-19 the party totals that shares were printed against were too small. Democrats: 257 where the refreshed roster has 258 on 2026-09-01 and 259 from 2026-09-02. Republicans: 269 where it has 271 on the 12 pages from 2026-11-04 to 2026-11-19. No Republican total printed before 2026-11-04 changes (the 2026-11-03 audit changes by one, but that page prints no total). These pages were assembled before 2026-11-21 and count voting members only, so they are compared with the refreshed roster's voting members; the five offices involved are all voting members. Each printed share was therefore slightly overstated. Computed over all 983 shares printed on those 55 pages, the largest difference is 0.08 percentage points (28 of 257, printed 10.9 percent, is 10.8 percent of 259, Democrats, 2026-09-11); 198 shares change in their printed decimal, none by more than 0.1 points. The same totals appear as counts, without a percentage, on 516 phrase pages whose peak day falls in the window. No ranking, threshold or selection used these totals, so no phrase or Daily Line changes.
corrections.detection_method: Read-only audit of the 120th Congress turnover (AUDIT-120th), then measured by rebuilding the roster from unitedstates/congress-legislators at revision a263880 and comparing every published day's denominator with the refreshed one.
corrections.resolution: The roster is refreshed from congress-legislators at revision a263880e99a78b8cfaf0a2487e05558be389de3d, recorded with both source file hashes. A party switch is now effective on its recorded date, which adds one Republican office from 2025-01-03 to 2026-03-08 (CA-3, recorded Independent from 2026-03-09); no published page used that range. From the first day assembled after this entry the totals are 262 Democratic and 274 Republican offices, delegates included. Published day records and their audits are not rewritten; this entry is linked from each listed day. The next refresh is due when upstream lists the 120th Congress; until then pages dated from 2027-01-03 print counts without a total.
corrections.root_cause: The count of a party's seated offices that pages print beside a share is read from a dated copy of the public congress-legislators roster. The copy in use was taken on 2026-07-27 and was not refreshed. Upstream has since added two House members who took office on 2026-09-01 (GA-13) and 2026-09-02 (CA-14), extended one Ohio Senate term from 2026-11-03 to 2026-12-15, and added a new Florida Senate term from 2026-11-04 for the senator whose appointed term ended on 2026-11-03.
